method: Direct visual inspection of each complete selected sheet; exact nav geometry is not certified.

M01.observation: Archive loading court, separated dormant Well and vitrified shoulders are visible; the three lower panels retain loading furniture, glass/basalt edge and Matter. No mission-coordinate or access proof is inferred.

M02.observation: Corrected sills are worked stone without civic electronics. Pale grass, compressed route margins and central basalt divider remain distinct. Actual route availability and grass scale need later map binding.

M03.observation: Distributed cistern, ribbed transit and archive service forms are distinguishable; lower studies expose paired duct mouths/grille, deck/coffer/gallery and cassette/service panels. Discharge water is a service-detail proposal, not a new terrain hazard.

M04.observation: Corrected vaults and docks use continuous grown strata, rooted grips and amber contacts. Earlier masonry/mechanical interpretation is superseded. The terminal custody niche is shown without claiming memory restoration.

M05.observation: Neutral corridor and offset witnesses remain distinct. Corrected mineral bench/spine contacts use amber; ceramic fittings retain cyan. The long corridor is a composition, not evidence of exact navigable width.

M06.observation: Monument-like props and incidental Well-like spire were removed; empty foundations, intact civic blocks and diagonal absence remain. Duct cross sections are visible in lower-left detail. No cause, deaths or population total is asserted.

M07.observation: Ridge sockets and ribs now use grown/stratified mineral forms. Hollow is empty; no incidental Well remains. Civic absence stays distant; witness approaches are visible without a branch-route acceptance claim.

M08.observation: Contact surface is now a low rectangular plinth distinct from the Future Well. Offset frame ends and solid terrace floors remain visible; endpoint material refinements and exact interaction footprint remain future work.

M09.observation: Two district branches visibly carry cyan status; Archive frontage is intact and dark. This is explicitly the illustrative Life Support + Transit allocation, not canon selection.

M10.observation: Corrected frontage is long, low and stepped; deferred Archive indicators remain dark and intact. Civic-mineral adapter uses amber on mineral side, distinct from magenta Choir panes. One dormant Well remains separate. Well failure-state authority conflict is unresolved.

M11.observation: Corrected Census Gate is a low rectilinear civic frontage. Two contribution settings, separate ceramic/mineral evidence stations and rally pad are visible; mineral record uses amber. Ornamental trees and banners were removed. No record text, deaths or faction merger is asserted.

M12.observation: Corrected Reserve Gate is a low civic frontage on a dry basalt plateau. Instrument line and independent ceramic/mineral readbacks remain distinct; mineral contact is amber and the separate Well is dormant. Repeated instrument counts in art are illustrative, not executable site bindings.

M13.observation: Blank horizontal index drawers, separate receivers and two empty witness platforms are visible. Incidental Well-like object was removed; mineral receiver now uses amber. No named dead, blame or restoration claim.

M14.observation: Distinct basin terraces, phase frames, command position, research table and unoccupied anchor setting are visible. Small central peg is an alignment detail candidate, not an installed crisis machine. No actual hold or failure behavior is evidenced.

M15.observation: Broken stellar fragments replace the eclipse, visible substructure grounds the dais, and empty resolution mount selects no ending. Three distinct construction-language sites and corresponding detail fittings remain visible. Fine signal colors and exact conduit silhouettes require later selected-state references.

SK01.observation: Corrected overview shows opposed north/south home shelves, three distinct crossing treatments, six cyan-white deposit clusters and one low dormant Well. Image is an abstract composition; actual path widths, ridge passability and travel-time fairness are not certified.

SK02.observation: Two north-south ridges now have six visible openings aligned into three east-west corridors. Eight Matter clusters and one north-of-center dormant Well are visible. Exact deposit zoning, coordinates, passage widths and fairness remain unverified; source/runtime Well-coordinate drift is recorded as MAP-DEC-008.

SK03.observation: Corrected overview shows four cardinal ring entrances, eight visible deposit clusters and one central Well. Base-like home ornaments were removed. Exact spawn/deposit zoning and approach fairness require registered-map verification.
